title.zh: 卷二百五十三 列傳第十二 折德扆 馮繼業 王承美 李繼周 孫行友
title.en: Volume 253 Biographies 12: Zhe Deyi, Feng Jiye, Wang Chengmei, Li Jizhou, Sun Xingyou
title.raw: 卷二百五十三 列傳第十二 折德扆 馮繼業 王承美 李繼周 孫行友 Volume 253 Biographies 12: Zhe Deyi, Feng Jiye, Wang Chengmei, Li Jizhou, Sun Xingyou

sentences.zh: 折德扆

translations.literal: Zhe Deyi
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Deyi

sentences.zh: 折德扆，世居雲中，為大族。

translations.literal: Zhe Deyi, for generations his family dwelt in Yunzhong and was a great clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Deyi came from a great clan that had lived in Yunzhong for generations.

sentences.zh: 父從阮，自晉、漢以來，獨據府州，控扼西北，中國賴之。

translations.literal: His father Congruan, from Jin and Han onward alone held Fuzhou, controlling and blocking the northwest; China relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Congruan had held Fuzhou alone since the Jin and Han dynasties, guarding the northwestern passes on which the realm depended.

sentences.zh: 仕周至靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: He served Zhou until becoming military commissioner of the Jingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he rose to military commissioner of the Jingnan Army.

sentences.zh: 其鎮府州時，署德扆為馬步軍都校。

translations.literal: When he governed Fuzhou, he appointed Deyi as chief commander of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Fuzhou he appointed Deyi chief commander of his cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 廣順間，周世宗建府州為永安軍，以德扆為節度使，時從阮鎮邠寧，父子俱領節鎮，時人榮之。

translations.literal: During Guangshun, Emperor Shizong of Zhou established Fuzhou as the Yong'an Army and made Deyi its military commissioner; at that time Congruan governed Binning—father and son both held commanderies, and people of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangshun era Emperor Shizong of Zhou made Fuzhou the Yong'an Army and appointed Deyi its military commissioner, while Congruan still held Binning—father and son both commanded frontier circuits, to the envy of their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，德扆率師攻下河市鎮，斬幷軍五百餘級。

translations.literal: In Xiande, Deyi led troops to attack and take Hexia Town, beheading more than five hundred Bing troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande reign Deyi led a force that captured Hexia Town and took more than five hundred heads among the Bing army.

sentences.zh: 入朝，以其弟德愿權總州事。

translations.literal: He entered court, and his younger brother Deyuan was put in temporary charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court and left his younger brother Deyuan in temporary charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時世宗南征，還次通許橋，德扆迎謁，且請遷內地。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Shizong was on a southern campaign and halted at Tongxu Bridge; Deyi came to meet him and also asked to be moved inland.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was returning from a southern campaign and stopped at Tongxu Bridge; Deyi came to pay his respects and asked to be transferred to an interior post.

sentences.zh: 世宗以其素得蕃情，不許，厚加賜賚而遣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because he had long won the hearts of the frontier peoples, did not permit it, richly rewarded him, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, saying Deyi was indispensable to frontier relations, but showered him with gifts before sending him home.

sentences.zh: 德扆未至，德愿又破幷軍五百餘於沙谷砦，斬其將郝章、張釗。

translations.literal: Before Deyi arrived, Deyuan again defeated more than five hundred Bing troops at Shagu Fort, beheading their generals Hao Zhang and Zhang Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Before Deyi returned, Deyuan routed another five hundred Bing troops at Shagu Fort and killed their commanders Hao Zhang and Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子 御勳

translations.literal: Son: Yu Xun
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yu Xun

sentences.zh: 御勳，字世隆，德扆鎮府州日，表為右職。

translations.literal: Yu Xun, style Shilong, when Deyi governed Fuzhou memorialized to appoint him to a senior post on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xun, courtesy name Shilong, was recommended for a senior staff post while his father Deyi governed Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 德扆卒，以御勳領汾州團練使、權知府州事。

translations.literal: When Deyi died, Yu Xun was made regimental trainer of Fenzhou and given temporary charge of Fuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyi died, Yu Xun was appointed regimental trainer of Fenzhou and put in temporary charge of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖征太原，御勳詣行在謁見，以為永安軍留後。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, Taizu campaigned against Taiyuan; Yu Xun went to the mobile court to pay respects and was made acting commissioner of the Yong'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 969, when Taizu marched on Taiyuan, Yu Xun came to the field headquarters and was named acting commissioner of the Yong'an Army.

sentences.zh: 四年，以郊祀來朝，禮畢歸鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he came to court for the suburban sacrifice; when the rites were finished he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he came to court for the suburban sacrifice and returned to his post when the rites ended.

sentences.zh: 九年，郊祀西洛，復來朝，道病後期，改泰寧軍節度使，留京師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the suburban sacrifice was at Western Luo; he came to court again, fell ill on the road and was late, was changed to military commissioner of the Taining Army, and was kept at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 976, when the sacrifice was held at Luoyang, he came again but fell ill en route and arrived late; he was reassigned as military commissioner of Taining and kept at the capital.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，卒，年四十，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he died, aged forty, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 977 at the age of forty and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子 御卿

translations.literal: Son: Yu Qing
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yu Qing

sentences.zh: 御卿，幼補節院使，御勳知州事，署為兵馬都校。

translations.literal: Yu Qing, while young was made an envoy of the military commission; when Yu Xun governed the prefecture he appointed him chief of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing entered service young as a military commission envoy; when Yu Xun governed the prefecture he named him chief of cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 御勳徙鎮，召為閑廄副使、知府州。

translations.literal: When Yu Xun was transferred to another command, Yu Qing was summoned as deputy commissioner of the spare stables and made prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Xun was transferred elsewhere, Yu Qing was summoned as deputy commissioner of the spare stables and appointed prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，命御卿與尹憲領屯兵同攻嵐州，又破岢嵐軍，擒其軍使折令圖以獻，遂下嵐州，又殺其憲州刺史霍翊，又擒其將馬延忠等七人。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned in Hedong he ordered Yu Qing and Yin Xian to lead garrison troops jointly to attack Lanzhou; they again defeated the Kela Army, captured its military commissioner Zhe Lingtu and presented him, then took Lanzhou, also killed its prefect Huo Yi, and also captured seven of its generals including Ma Yanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizong's Hedong campaign Yu Qing and Yin Xian were ordered to attack Lanzhou together; they routed the Kela garrison, captured its commander Zhe Lingtu, took the city, killed prefect Huo Yi, and seized seven officers including Ma Yanzhong.

sentences.zh: 遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commissioner of honored rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner of honored rites.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，凡四遷而為府州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, after four promotions in all he became observation commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By 992, after four promotions, he had become observation commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜永安軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed military commissioner of the Yong'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 994 he was appointed military commissioner of the Yong'an Army.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹眾萬餘入寇，御卿大敗之於子河氵義，斬首五千級，獲馬千匹，契丹將號突厥太尉、司徒、舍利死者二十餘人，擒其吐渾一人，自是契丹知所畏。

translations.literal: Soon after, more than ten thousand Khitan invaded; Yu Qing greatly defeated them at Zihe Yi, beheading five thousand, capturing a thousand horses; more than twenty Khitan officers titled Turkic Grand Captain, Minister, and Sheli died, and one Tuyuhun was captured—from then on the Khitan knew fear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward more than ten thousand Khitan raided; Yu Qing crushed them at Zihe Yi, taking five thousand heads and a thousand horses; more than twenty Khitan officers bearing titles such as Turkic Grand Captain, Minister, and Sheli were killed, and one Tuyuhun captive was taken—from then on the Khitan learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 太宗因遣使問御卿曰：「西北要害皆屯勁兵，戎人何自而至？」

translations.literal: Taizong therefore sent an envoy to ask Yu Qing: "All the vital points of the northwest are garrisoned with crack troops—how did the barbarians come on their own?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent an envoy to ask Yu Qing, "Every key point in the northwest is held by crack troops—how did the barbarians get through?"

sentences.zh: 御卿對曰：「敵緣山峽小徑入，謀剽略。

translations.literal: Yu Qing replied: "The enemy came in by a small path along the mountain gorge, intending to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing answered, "They slipped in by a narrow mountain track, intending to raid.

sentences.zh: 臣諜知之，遣人邀其歸路，因縱兵大擊，敗走之，人馬墜厓谷死者相忱，其大將韓德威僅以身免。

translations.literal: Your servant learned it by spies, sent men to block their return route, then unleashed troops in a great strike, routed and drove them off; men and horses falling into cliff gorges died piled upon one another; their great general Han Dewei barely escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: I learned of it through scouts and sent men to cut off their retreat, then struck hard and drove them off; men and horses fell dead in heaps in the ravines, and their commander Han Dewei barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 皆聖靈所及，非臣之功也。」

translations.literal: All was reached by your sacred spirit—it is not your servant's merit."
translations.idiomatic: It was all due to your sacred favor, not my merit."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，御卿被病，德威諜知之，且為李繼遷所誘，率眾來侵，以報子河氵義之役。

translations.literal: After more than a year Yu Qing fell ill; Dewei learned it by spies and, moreover incited by Li Jiqian, led a host to invade to avenge the battle of Zihe Yi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Yu Qing fell ill; Han Dewei learned of it through spies and, urged on by Li Jiqian, led a force to raid in revenge for Zihe Yi.

sentences.zh: 御卿力疾出戰，德威聞其至，不敢進。

translations.literal: Yu Qing forced himself, though ill, to go out to battle; when Dewei heard he had come, he did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing dragged himself from his sickbed to fight; when Han Dewei heard he had come out, he dared not press the attack.

sentences.zh: 會疾甚，其母密遣人召歸，御卿曰：「世受國恩，邊寇未滅，御卿罪也。

translations.literal: When his illness grew severe, his mother secretly sent someone to summon him home; Yu Qing said: "For generations we have received the state's grace; the border foe is not yet destroyed—that is Yu Qing's crime.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, his mother secretly sent for him to come home; Yu Qing said, "Our family has enjoyed the state's favor for generations; as long as the border enemy is unbeaten, I am the one at fault.

sentences.zh: 今臨敵棄士卒自便，不可，死於軍中乃其分也。

translations.literal: Now, facing the enemy, to abandon the troops for my own convenience cannot be done; to die in the army is my proper lot.
translations.idiomatic: To leave my men now that the enemy is here would be unthinkable; dying in the ranks is my proper duty.

sentences.zh: 為白太夫人，無念我，忠孝豈兩全！」

translations.literal: Tell the Grand Lady for me: do not think of me—loyalty and filial piety, how can both be complete!"
translations.idiomatic: Tell my mother not to worry about me—loyalty and filial duty cannot both be fulfilled!"

sentences.zh: 言訖泣下。

translations.literal: When he had spoken, tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he finished speaking.

sentences.zh: 翌日卒，年三十八。

translations.literal: The next day he died, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next day, at thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 上聞悼惜久之，贈侍中，以其子惟正為洛苑使、知州事。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he mourned and regretted for a long time, posthumously made him Palace Attendant, and appointed his son Weizheng as commissioner of the Luo Park and put him in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him at length, posthumously made him Palace Attendant, and appointed his son Weizheng commissioner of the Luo Park with charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 惟正歸朝，以其弟惟昌繼之。

translations.literal: Weizheng returned to court, and his younger brother Weichang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Weizheng went to court, his younger brother Weichang succeeded him in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，表求赴闕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he memorialized asking to come to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1009 he petitioned to come to court.

sentences.zh: 真宗命近臣與射於苑中，宴賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Zhenzong ordered close ministers to shoot with him in the park and feasted and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong had his close ministers join him in archery in the imperial park and entertained Weichang with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 上言：「先臣御卿蒙賜旗三十竿以壯軍容，請別給賜。」

translations.literal: He submitted: "My late father Yu Qing received the gift of thirty banner poles to strengthen military display; I ask for a separate grant."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "My late father Yu Qing was granted thirty banner poles to enhance his troops' appearance; I ask for a grant of my own."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 七年，命河東民運糧赴麟州，當出兵為援，惟昌力疾領步騎屯寧遠砦，冒風沙而行。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the people of Hedong were ordered to transport grain to Linzhou; troops were to be sent in support; Weichang, forcing himself though ill, led infantry and cavalry to garrison Ningyuan Fort, marching through wind and sand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1014, when Hedong civilians were ordered to haul grain to Linzhou, Weichang, though seriously ill, led foot and horse to garrison Ningyuan Fort and marched through wind and sand to support them.

sentences.zh: 時疾已亟，猶與賓佐宴飲，談笑自若焉。

translations.literal: Though his illness was already severe, he still feasted and drank with guests and staff, talking and laughing as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Though his illness was grave, he still feasted with his staff, talking and laughing as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 明日卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: The next day he died, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next day, at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 以其弟惟忠繼之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Weizhong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Weizhong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 惟忠，字藎臣，初以兄惟信戰沒，補西頭供奉官，擢閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Weizhong, style Jinchen, at first because his elder brother Weixin died in battle was made a western-head palace attendant, and was promoted to gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong, courtesy name Jinchen, entered service as a western-head palace attendant after his elder brother Weixin was killed in battle and was promoted to gate usher.

sentences.zh: 及惟昌卒，以惟忠為六宅使、知府州兼麟府路都巡檢使，領普州刺史；

translations.literal: When Weichang died, Weizhong was made commissioner of the Six Residences, prefect of Fuzhou and overall inspector of the Lin-Fu circuit, and held the prefecture of Puzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Weichang died, Weizhong was made commissioner of the Six Residences, prefect of Fuzhou, and overall inspector of the Lin-Fu circuit, while also holding the prefecture of Puzhou;

sentences.zh: 再遷左藏庫使，真拜嘉州刺史，改資州，進簡州團練使。

translations.literal: he was again promoted to commissioner of the left treasury, truly appointed prefect of Jiazhou, changed to Zizhou, and advanced to regimental trainer of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: he was later promoted to commissioner of the left treasury, confirmed as prefect of Jiazhou, transferred to Zizhou, and advanced to regimental trainer of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 喪母，起復雲麾將軍，卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning as Cloud-Banner General and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning as Cloud-Banner General and later died in office.

sentences.zh: 惟忠知兵事。

translations.literal: Weizhong understood military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong was skilled in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，契丹與夏國會兵境上，聲言嫁娶，惟忠覘得其實，率麾下往備之，戒士卒毋輕動。

translations.literal: In Tiansheng, Khitan and Xia joined forces on the border, proclaiming a marriage alliance; Weizhong spied out the truth, led his subordinates to prepare against them, and warned the troops not to move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era the Khitan and Xia massed on the border under the pretense of a marriage alliance; Weizhong discovered their real intent, led his men to meet them, and ordered his troops not to stir rashly.

sentences.zh: 一夕風霾，有騎走營中，以為寇至，惟忠堅臥不動，徐命擒之，得數誕馬，蓋虜所縱也。

translations.literal: One night in wind and haze, mounted men ran through the camp; they thought the raiders had come; Weizhong lay firm and did not move, slowly ordered them seized, and got several stray horses—it turned out the barbarians had released them.
translations.idiomatic: One night in a sandstorm riders dashed through the camp and men cried that the enemy had come; Weizhong lay still, then calmly ordered them caught—it proved to be a few stray horses the barbarians had turned loose.

sentences.zh: 既卒，錄其弟侄子孫七人，以其子繼宣嗣州事。

translations.literal: When he died, seven of his younger brothers, nephews, and grandsons were enrolled in office, and his son Jixuan succeeded to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After his death seven younger kinsmen—brothers, nephews, and grandsons—were given posts, and his son Jixuan succeeded to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，特贈惟忠耀州觀察使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was specially posthumously made observation commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was posthumously made observation commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 寶元中，繼宣坐苛虐掊刻，種落嗟怨，絀為左監門衛將軍、楚州都監，擢其弟右侍禁繼閔為西京作坊使，嗣州事。

translations.literal: In Baoyuan, Jixuan sat in guilt for harsh cruelty and extortion; the tribes sighed in resentment; he was demoted to general of the Left Gate Guard and military supervisor of Chuzhou; his younger brother, right palace guard Jiyin, was promoted to commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and succeeded to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoyuan era Jixuan was punished for harsh extortion that alienated the tribes; he was demoted to general of the Left Gate Guard and military supervisor of Chuzhou, while his younger brother Jiyin, a right palace guard, was made commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and succeeded him at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 繼閔，字廣孝。

translations.literal: Jiyin, style Guangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin, courtesy name Guangxiao.

sentences.zh: 慶歷中，元昊兵攻麟州不克，進圍州城。

translations.literal: In Qingli, Yuan Hao's troops attacked Linzhou without success and advanced to besiege the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era Yuan Hao's army failed to take Linzhou and instead laid siege to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 城險且堅，東南有水門，厓壁峭絕，阻河。

translations.literal: The city was perilous and firm; to the southeast was a water gate; cliff walls were steep and absolute, blocked by the river.
translations.idiomatic: The city was strong and well defended; on the southeast was a water gate where cliffs dropped sheer to the river.

sentences.zh: 賊緣厓腹微徑魚貫而前，城中矢石亂下，賊轉攻城北，士卒復力戰，賊死傷甚眾，遂引去，圍豐州，豐州遂陷。

translations.literal: The bandits followed a slight path along the cliff belly in single file; from the city arrows and stones rained down in disorder; the bandits turned to attack the north of the city; the troops again fought fiercely; the bandits died and were wounded in great numbers, then withdrew; they besieged Fengzhou, and Fengzhou then fell.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy crept along a narrow ledge in single file; the defenders rained arrows and stones upon them; when the attackers shifted to the north wall the garrison fought them off again with heavy losses to the enemy, who then withdrew to besiege Fengzhou, which soon fell.

sentences.zh: 繼閔以城守勞，特遷宮苑使、普州刺史。

translations.literal: Jiyin, for his labor in defending the city, was specially promoted to commissioner of the palace park and prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his defense of the city Jiyin was specially promoted to commissioner of the palace park and prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，護送麟州戍卒冬服，賊伏兵邀擊之，盡掠所賫，繼閔脫身繇間道歸。

translations.literal: Before long, escorting winter clothing for the Linzhou garrison, the bandits ambushed them, plundered all they carried, and Jiyin escaped by a bypath and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, while escorting winter uniforms for the Linzhou garrison, he was ambushed and everything he carried was seized; Jiyin escaped by a back trail.

sentences.zh: 會赦，止奪宮苑使，後復官，領果州團練使。

translations.literal: An amnesty intervened; only his post as palace park commissioner was taken; later his office was restored and he held regimental trainer of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared him further punishment—only his palace park commission was removed—and he was later restored to office as regimental trainer of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 自元昊反，繼閔招輯歸業者三千餘戶。

translations.literal: From Yuan Hao's rebellion, Jiyin gathered and settled more than three thousand households returning to their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao's rebellion Jiyin resettled more than three thousand households who returned to farming.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年，卒，以其弟繼祖嗣州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangyou he died, and his younger brother Jizu succeeded to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1050, and his younger brother Jizu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 繼祖，字應之，由右侍禁遷西染院使，累轉皇城使、成州團練使。

translations.literal: Jizu, style Yingzhi, from right palace guard was moved to commissioner of the western dyeing court, and through repeated promotions became imperial city commissioner and regimental trainer of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu, courtesy name Yingzhi, rose from right palace guard to commissioner of the western dyeing court and eventually to imperial city commissioner and regimental trainer of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨政二十餘年。

translations.literal: He governed for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the prefecture for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 奏乞書籍，仁宗賜以《九經》。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging for books; Renzong granted him the Nine Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for books, and Renzong granted him the Nine Classics.

sentences.zh: 韓絳發河東兵城囉兀，繼祖為先鋒，深入敵帳，降部落戶八百。

translations.literal: Han Jiang mobilized Hedong troops to fortify Luowu; Jizu was vanguard, penetrated deep into the enemy camp, and received the surrender of eight hundred tribal households.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang sent Hedong troops to build a fort at Luowu, Jizu led the vanguard deep into enemy territory and received the surrender of eight hundred tribal households.

sentences.zh: 加解州防禦使，卒。

translations.literal: He was added as defense commissioner of Jiezhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was made defense commissioner of Jiezhou and later died.

sentences.zh: 繼祖有子當襲州事，請以授兄之子克柔，詔從之，而進其三子官，錄二孫為借職。

translations.literal: Jizu had a son who should have inherited prefectural affairs; he asked to give it to his elder brother's son Kerou; an edict followed his request, while his three sons were advanced in office and two grandsons were enrolled as borrowed posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu had a son entitled to succeed him but asked that the post go to his elder brother's son Kerou; the throne approved, promoted his three sons, and enrolled two grandsons in borrowed posts.

sentences.zh: 弟繼世，少從軍，為延州東路巡檢。

translations.literal: Younger brother Jishi, from youth followed the army and was eastern-route inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jishi entered the army young and became eastern-route inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嵬名山之內附，繼世先知之，遣其子克懃報种諤，諤用是取綏州。

translations.literal: When Weiming Shan came over to the interior, Jishi knew it first, sent his son Keqin to report to Chong Shi, and Shi by this took Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiming Shan defected, Jishi learned of it first and sent his son Keqin to inform Chong Shi, who thereby captured Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 繼世以騎步萬軍於懷寧砦，入晉祠谷，往銀川，分名山之眾萬五千戶居於大理河。

translations.literal: Jishi with ten thousand horse and foot at Huaining Fort entered Jinci Valley, went to Yinchuan, and divided Weiming Shan's multitude of fifteen thousand households to dwell on the Dali River.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi led ten thousand cavalry and infantry from Huaining Fort through Jinci Valley to Yinchuan and resettled fifteen thousand of Weiming Shan's followers along the Dali River.

sentences.zh: 夏人來攻，再戰皆捷。

translations.literal: The Xia people came to attack; twice they fought and both were victories.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut attacked, he fought them twice and won both times.

sentences.zh: 諤抵罪逮繫獄，以兵付之而行，遂同名山守綏州，綠功領忠州刺史。

translations.literal: Shi was charged with crime and imprisoned; troops were handed to Jishi and he set out, then together with Weiming Shan guarded Suizhou, and for merit held the prefecture of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong Shi was imprisoned on criminal charges, Jishi was given his troops and, together with Weiming Shan, held Suizhou; for his service he was made prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 說韓絳城囉兀以撫橫山，因畫取河南之策，絳以為然。

translations.literal: He persuaded Han Jiang to fortify Luowu to pacify Hengshan, and thereby drew up a plan to seize the lands south of the river; Jiang thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded Han Jiang to build Luowu to pacify the Hengshan region and outlined a plan to seize territory south of the Yellow River, which Han Jiang accepted.

sentences.zh: 以左騏驥使、果州團練使卒。

translations.literal: He died as left commissioner of fine horses and regimental trainer of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as left commissioner of fine horses and regimental trainer of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 諸司使無賻禮，詔以繼世蕃官，捍邊有績，特給之。

translations.literal: Commissioners of the various bureaus had no funeral gift by rule; an edict said that because Jishi was a frontier tribal official who had merit defending the border, it was specially granted.
translations.idiomatic: Palace commissioners normally received no funeral gifts by regulation, but an edict specially granted one to Jishi as a frontier tribal officer who had distinguished himself on the border.

sentences.zh: 從子克行。

translations.literal: Nephew: Kexing.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Kexing

sentences.zh: 曾孫 克行

translations.literal: Great-grandson: Kexing
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson: Kexing

sentences.zh: 克行，字遵道，繼閔子也。

translations.literal: Kexing, style Zundao, was Jiyin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Kexing, courtesy name Zundao, was the son of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 初仕軍府，無所知名。

translations.literal: At first he served in the military commission and was not known for anything.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the military commission without attracting notice.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇環慶，种諤拒之，詔河東出師為援，克行請往。

translations.literal: The Xia people raided Huanqing; Chong Shi resisted them; an edict ordered Hedong to send troops in support; Kexing asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Huanqing and Chong Shi held them off, the court ordered Hedong to send reinforcements; Kexing volunteered.

sentences.zh: 諤使以兵三千護餉道，戰於葭蘆川，先登，斬級四百，降戶千，馬畜萬計。

translations.literal: Shi sent him with three thousand troops to guard the supply route; they fought at Jialu River; he was first to ascend, beheaded four hundred, received the surrender of a thousand households, and horses and livestock numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Shi gave him three thousand men to guard the supply line; at Jialu River he led the assault, took four hundred heads, received the surrender of a thousand households, and captured tens of thousands of horses and livestock.

sentences.zh: 諸老將矍然曰：「真折太尉子也！」

translations.literal: The veteran generals started and said: "Truly the son of Grand Captain Zhe!"
translations.idiomatic: The veteran generals exclaimed, "He is truly a son of Grand Captain Zhe!"

sentences.zh: 擢知府州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to govern Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦兵討夏國，張世矩將河外軍民，克行與俱。

translations.literal: Qin troops campaigned against the Xia state; Zhang Shiju commanded the army and people beyond the river; Kexing went with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin forces campaigned against the Xia, Zhang Shiju commanded the army and civilians beyond the river, and Kexing marched with him.

sentences.zh: 廷議謂守臣難自行，詔克行選兵隸世矩。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that border defenders could hardly act on their own; an edict ordered Kexing to select troops and place them under Shiju.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that frontier commanders could not campaign on their own and ordered Kexing to detach troops under Zhang Shiju's command.

sentences.zh: 克行抗章，願率部落先驅，未報，即委管鑰而西。

translations.literal: Kexing submitted a memorial in protest, wishing to lead the tribes as vanguard; before a reply came, he entrusted the keys of office and went west.
translations.idiomatic: Kexing protested in a memorial that he wished to lead his tribes as vanguard; receiving no answer, he turned over the seals of office and marched west on his own.

sentences.zh: 大酋咩保吳良以萬騎來躡，克行為後拒，度賊半度隘，縱擊大破之，殺咩保吳良。

translations.literal: The great chieftain Miebao Wuliang came with ten thousand horse to pursue; Kexing served as rear guard; estimating the bandits half through the pass, he unleashed a strike and greatly defeated them, killing Miebao Wuliang.
translations.idiomatic: The great chieftain Miebao Wuliang pursued with ten thousand horsemen; Kexing covered the rear and, waiting until half the enemy had passed the defile, struck and routed them, killing Miebao Wuliang.

sentences.zh: 師還自劾，釋不問。

translations.literal: When the army returned he impeached himself, and was released without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he submitted a self-accusation, which the court dismissed without punishment.

sentences.zh: 王中正出塞，克行先拔宥州，每出必勝，夏人畏之，益左廂兵，專以當折氏。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongzheng went beyond the passes; Kexing first took Youzhou; every time he went out he was sure to win; the Xia people feared him and increased the left wing army, specially to oppose the Zhe clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhongzheng campaigned beyond the border, Kexing was first to take Youzhou; he won every engagement, and the Tangut, fearing him, reinforced their left wing army specifically to counter the Zhe family.

sentences.zh: 太原孫覽議城葭蘆，諸將論多不合，召克行問策，即頓兵吐渾河，約勒部伍，為深入窮討之狀，敵疑不敢動。

translations.literal: Sun Lan of Taiyuan proposed fortifying Jialu; the generals' discussions mostly did not agree; Kexing was summoned to ask his plan; he immediately halted troops at the Tuhun River, disciplined his units, and made a show of deep advance and thorough pursuit; the enemy suspected and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Lan of Taiyuan proposed building a fort at Jialu and the generals could not agree, Kexing was summoned for advice; he halted his army on the Tuhun River, drilled his men, and feigned a deep pursuit that kept the enemy from stirring.

sentences.zh: 既訖役，又入津慶、龍橫川，斬級三千。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he again entered Jinqing and Longheng River, beheading three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort was finished he raided Jinqing and Longheng River and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 詔河東進築八砦，通道鄜延。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hedong to advance and build eight forts, opening a route to Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Hedong to build eight advance forts and open a route to Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 延帥遣秦希甫來共議，克行請兩路併力，以遠者為先，希甫曰：「由近及遠，法也。」

translations.literal: The Fuyan commander sent Qin Xifu to discuss together; Kexing asked that the two routes combine strength and take the distant first; Xifu said: "From near to far—that is the method."
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyan commander sent Qin Xifu to consult; Kexing urged both circuits to combine forces and build the distant forts first; Xifu said, "From near to far—that is the proper method."

sentences.zh: 克行曰：「不然，事有奇正。

translations.literal: Kexing said: "Not so—affairs have orthodox and unorthodox aspects.
translations.idiomatic: Kexing replied, "Not so—there is orthodox strategy and there is unorthodox strategy.

sentences.zh: 今乘士氣之銳，所利在速，故先遠役，以出其不意，若徐圖之，士心且怠矣。」

translations.literal: Now, riding the sharpness of the troops' morale, what profits us is speed; therefore we work the distant posts first, to take them unawares—if we plan slowly, the soldiers' hearts will slacken."
translations.idiomatic: Our men are at peak morale and speed is everything, so we should build the distant forts first and catch the enemy off guard; if we proceed slowly, their fighting spirit will fade."

sentences.zh: 希甫持不可，並上二議，卒用克行策。

translations.literal: Xifu held that it could not be done; both memorials were submitted, and in the end Kexing's plan was used.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu objected, but both plans went to the throne and Kexing's strategy was adopted.

sentences.zh: 城成，諜言寇至，軍中皆戒嚴，克行止之曰：「彼自擾耳。」

translations.literal: When the fort was completed, spies reported that bandits had come; the army all went on alert; Kexing stopped them and said: "They are only stirring themselves up."
translations.idiomatic: When the fort was finished, scouts reported an enemy approach and the army went on alert; Kexing stopped them, saying, "They are only rattling themselves."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it proved exactly so.

sentences.zh: 克行在邊三十年，善拊士卒，戰功最多，羌人呼為『折家父』。

translations.literal: Kexing was on the border thirty years, was good at comforting troops, and had the most battle merit; the Qiang called him "Father of the Zhe House."
translations.idiomatic: Kexing served on the frontier for thirty years, won his soldiers' loyalty, and accumulated more battle honors than any of his kin; the Qiang called him "Father of the Zhe clan."

sentences.zh: 官至秦州觀察使，卒，贈武安軍節度使。

translations.literal: His office reached observation commissioner of Qinzhou; he died and was posthumously made military commissioner of the Wu'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to observation commissioner of Qinzhou and, on his death, was posthumously made military commissioner of the Wu'an Army.

sentences.zh: 子可大為榮州團練使、知府州。

translations.literal: His son Kedà was made regimental trainer of Rongzhou and prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kedà became regimental trainer of Rongzhou and prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 從子可適。

translations.literal: Nephew: Keshi.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Keshi

sentences.zh: 可適未冠有勇，馳射不習而能。

translations.literal: Keshi, before the cap was full, had courage; in mounted archery he could do it without study.
translations.idiomatic: Keshi was brave before he came of age and could shoot from horseback without formal training.

sentences.zh: 鄜延郭逵見之，歎曰：「真將種也！」

translations.literal: Guo Kui of Fuyan saw him and sighed: "Truly the seed of a general!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Kui of Fuyan saw him and exclaimed, "He is born to be a general!"

sentences.zh: 薦試廷中，補殿侍，隸延州。

translations.literal: He was recommended for trial at court, made a palace attendant, and attached to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for examination at court, he was made a palace attendant and assigned to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 從种諤出塞，遇敵馬以少年易之，可適索與鬥，斬其首，取馬而還，益知名，米脂之役，與夏人戰三角嶺，得級多，又敗之於蒲桃谷東。

translations.literal: Following Chong Shi beyond the passes, he met enemy horsemen who belittled him for his youth; Keshi demanded to duel, beheaded the man, took his horse and returned, and became still better known; in the Mizhi campaign he fought the Xia at Sanjiao Ridge and took many heads, and again defeated them east of Putao Valley.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign with Chong Shi beyond the border, he met enemy horsemen who mocked his youth; Keshi challenged one to single combat, cut off his head, seized his horse, and rode back to growing fame; at Mizhi he fought the Tangut at Sanjiao Ridge with many kills and routed them again east of Putao Valley.

sentences.zh: 兵久不得食，千人成聚，籍籍於軍門，或欲掩殺以為功，可適曰：「此以饑而逃耳，非叛也。」

translations.literal: The army had long gone without food; a thousand men gathered in a mob, clamoring at the army gate; some wished to slaughter them for merit; Keshi said: "These fled from hunger—it is not rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: After long hunger a thousand men clustered at headquarters clamoring for food, and some officers wanted to slaughter them for credit; Keshi said, "They are starving deserters, not mutineers."

sentences.zh: 單馬出詰之曰：「爾輩何至是，不為父母妻子念而甘心為異域鬼耶？」

translations.literal: He went out alone on horseback to reprove them: "Why have you come to this—do you not think of parents, wives, and children, yet willingly become ghosts in a foreign land?"
translations.idiomatic: He rode out alone and rebuked them: "How can you do this—have you no thought for your parents, wives, and children, yet choose to die as ghosts in enemy country?"

sentences.zh: 皆回面聲喏，流涕謝再生，各遣歸。

translations.literal: All turned their faces, voiced assent, wept and thanked him for renewed life, and each was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: They turned, shouted assent, wept and thanked him for their lives, and were sent home one by one.

sentences.zh: 羌、夏人十萬入寇，可適先得其守烽卒姓名，詐為首領行視，呼出塞斬之，烽不傳，因卷甲疾趨，大破之於尾丁磑。

translations.literal: Qiang and Xia, a hundred thousand, invaded; Keshi first obtained the names of their beacon guards, pretended to be a chieftain on inspection, called them out beyond the pass and beheaded them, beacons did not transmit, and he therefore rolled up armor and hurried, greatly defeating them at Weiding Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When a hundred thousand Qiang and Tangut invaded, Keshi learned the names of their beacon guards, posed as a chieftain on inspection, lured them beyond the pass and killed them so no alarm was sent, then marched swiftly and crushed them at Weiding Wei.

sentences.zh: 回次檉楊溝，正午駐營，分騎據西山，曰：「彼若躡吾後，腹背受敵，必敗。」

translations.literal: Returning, he halted at Chenyang Gully; at noon he encamped and divided horsemen to hold the western hills, saying: "If they follow our rear, caught front and back, they are sure to be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he camped at Chenyang Gully at noon and posted cavalry on the western hills, saying, "If they follow us we will catch them between two forces and they cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 果舉軍來，可適所部𦆵八千，轉戰至高嶺，廼從間道趣洪德，設伏邀其歸路。

translations.literal: Indeed the whole army came; Keshi's command of only eight thousand fought in turn up to Gaoling, then by a bypath hastened to Hongde and set an ambush on their return route.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy army came as he had foreseen; with only eight thousand men Keshi fought his way to Gaoling, then slipped by a back trail to Hongde and laid an ambush on their retreat.

sentences.zh: 敵至，伏發衝之，其國母窬山而遁，焚棄輜重，雖帷賬首飾之屬亦不返，眾相蹈藉，赴厓澗死者如積。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived, the ambush burst forth and struck them; their queen mother fled over the mountains; they burned and abandoned baggage; even curtain hangings and head ornaments were not taken back; the masses trampled one another; those who fell into cliff gullies died piled like heaps.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived the ambush struck; their queen mother fled over the mountains; they abandoned and burned their baggage, leaving even curtains and ornaments behind; the fugitives trampled one another and died in heaps in the ravines.

sentences.zh: 論前後功，至皇城使、成州團練使、知岷蘭州鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: Tallying merit before and after, he reached imperial city commissioner, regimental trainer of Chengzhou, and governed Minzhou, Lanzhou, and Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: For his cumulative service he rose to imperial city commissioner, regimental trainer of Chengzhou, and commander of Minzhou, Lanzhou, and Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 渭帥章楶合熙、秦、慶三道兵築好水川，命總管王文振統之，而可適將軍為副。

translations.literal: Commander Zhang Jie of Wei combined the Xi, Qin, and Qing circuits' troops to fortify Haoshui River; he ordered overall commander Wang Wenzhen to command them, with Keshi as deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie, commander of Wei, combined troops from the Xi, Qin, and Qing circuits to build a fort at Haoshui River, with Wang Wenzhen as overall commander and Keshi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 熙州兵千人失道盡死，文振歸罪於可適，楶即下之吏，宰相章惇欲按軍法，哲宗不許，猶削十三官而罷。

translations.literal: A thousand troops of Xizhou lost their way and all died; Wenzhen placed the blame on Keshi; Jie immediately had him handed to the law officers; Chancellor Zhang Dun wished to punish by military law; Zhezong did not permit it, but still stripped thirteen ranks and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand Xizhou troops lost their way and perished; Wenzhen blamed Keshi, and Jie had him arrested; Chancellor Zhang Dun wanted him executed under military law, but Zhezong refused, though he still stripped thirteen ranks and removed him from command.

sentences.zh: 楶請留以責效，乃以權第十二將。

translations.literal: Jie asked to keep him to answer for results, and he was then made acting commander of the Twelfth Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: Jie asked to retain him until he could prove himself, and he was made acting commander of the Twelfth Regiment.

sentences.zh: 嵬名阿埋、昧勒都逋，皆夏人桀黠用事者，詔可適密圖之，會二酋以畜牧為名會境上，可適諜知之，遣兵夜往襲，並俘其族屬三千人，遂取天都山。

translations.literal: Weiming Amai and Mile Dupo were both Xia men, fierce and crafty and in power; an edict ordered Keshi to plot against them secretly; it happened the two chieftains met on the border in the name of pasturing livestock; Keshi learned it by spies, sent troops by night to strike, and captured their clansmen, three thousand in all, then took Tiandu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Weiming Amai and Mile Dupo were powerful, cunning Tangut leaders; the court ordered Keshi to eliminate them; when the two met on the border under pretense of grazing livestock, Keshi learned of it through spies, raided by night, captured three thousand of their kin, and took Tiandu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝為御文德殿受賀，以其地為西安州，遷可適東上閤門使、洺州防禦使、涇原鈐轄、知州事，真拜和州防禦使，進明州觀察使，為副都總管。

translations.literal: The emperor received congratulations in the Wende Hall; that place was made Xi'anzhou; Keshi was moved to eastern upper gate envoy, defense commissioner of Mingzhou, Jingyuan commander, and prefect; truly appointed defense commissioner of Hezhou, advanced to observation commissioner of Mingzhou, and made deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received congratulations in the Wende Hall and made the region Xi'anzhou; Keshi was promoted to eastern upper gate envoy, defense commissioner of Mingzhou, Jingyuan commander, and prefect, then confirmed as defense commissioner of Hezhou and observation commissioner of Mingzhou, and made deputy overall commander.

sentences.zh: 帥鐘傳行邊，為敵所隔，以輕騎拔之，得歸。

translations.literal: Commander Zhong Chuan was on a border tour and was cut off by the enemy; with light cavalry Keshi rescued him and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander Zhong Chuan was cut off on a border tour, Keshi broke through with light cavalry and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 傳議取靈武，環慶，亦請出師，命可適將萬騎往，即薄靈州川。

translations.literal: Chuan discussed taking Lingwu and Huanqing; he also asked to send troops; Keshi was ordered to lead ten thousand horse and went immediately close to Lingzhou River.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan proposed taking Lingwu and Huanqing and requested reinforcements; Keshi was ordered to lead ten thousand horsemen and advanced to the banks of the Lingzhou River.

sentences.zh: 夏人扶老挾稚，中夜入州城，明日俘獲甚夥，而慶兵不至，乃引還。

translations.literal: The Xia people, supporting the old and leading the young, entered the prefectural city at midnight; the next day captives were very many, but Qing troops did not arrive, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut, old and young together, entered the city at midnight; the next day his captives were many, but Qing reinforcements never came and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔使人覲，帝以傳策訪焉，對曰：「得之易，守之難，當先侵弱其地，待吾藩籬既固，然後可圖。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to come to audience; the emperor consulted him on Chuan's plan; he replied: "Taking it is easy, holding it hard—we should first weaken their territory by gradual encroachment; when our defensive screen is firm, then we may plan."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was asked about Chuan's plan and answered, "It is easy to take but hard to hold; we should first wear down their territory and only when our frontier defenses are solid plan a full conquest."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 進武安軍節度觀察留後、步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was advanced to military commissioner and observation acting commissioner of the Wu'an Army and chief adjutant of the foot army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military commissioner and observation acting commissioner of the Wu'an Army and chief adjutant of the foot army.

sentences.zh: 大城蕭關，與傳議齟齬，會覆師數百於踏口，傳劾之，貶鄭州觀察使。

translations.literal: He greatly fortified Xiaoguan, clashed with Chuan in counsel, and when several hundred troops were destroyed at Tako, Chuan impeached him and he was demoted to observation commissioner of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He built up Xiaoguan, quarreled with Chuan over strategy, and when several hundred men were lost at Tako, Chuan impeached him and he was demoted to observation commissioner of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄知衛州，拜淮康軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Weizhou and appointed military commissioner of the Huai'kang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Weizhou and military commissioner of the Huai'kang Army.

sentences.zh: 轉運使請於平夏、通峽、鎮戎、西安四砦分築場圃，置芻粟五百萬，可適以費大難之，又欲借車牛以運，及致十萬斛於熙河，皆戾其意，乃中以疑謗，召為佑神觀使。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner asked to build separate stockyards at the four forts of Pingxia, Tongxia, Zhenrong, and Xi'an, setting five million bundles of fodder; Keshi objected that the expense was too great; he also wished to borrow carts and oxen to transport, and to deliver a hundred thousand hu to Xihe—all contrary to his intent; he was then struck with suspicion and slander, and was summoned as commissioner of the Youshen Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner proposed stockyards at four forts with five million bundles of fodder; Keshi protested the cost, refused to lend carts and oxen, and balked at shipping a hundred thousand hu to Xihe; enemies slandered him and he was recalled as commissioner of the Youshen Observatory.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以為渭州，命其子彥質直秘閣參軍事，數月而卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: The next year he was again made commander of Wei; his son Yanzhi was made a direct secretary in the Secretariat; after several months he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again appointed to Wei; his son Yanzhi was made a direct secretary in the Secretariat; he died several months later at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 彥質，紹興中簽書樞密院，別有傳。

translations.literal: Yanzhi, in the Shaoxing era, signed the Bureau of Military Affairs—treated in a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi later signed the Bureau of Military Affairs in the Shaoxing era and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 馮繼業

translations.literal: Feng Jiye
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jiye

sentences.zh: 馮繼業，字嗣宗，大名人。

translations.literal: Feng Jiye, style Sizong, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jiye, courtesy name Sizong, was a native of Daming.

sentences.zh: 父暉，朔方節度，封衛王。

translations.literal: His father Hui was military commissioner of Shuofang and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was military commissioner of Shuofang and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 繼業幼敏慧，有度量，以父任補朔方軍節院使，隨父歷邠、孟，及再領朔方，皆補牙職。

translations.literal: Jiye in youth was clever and intelligent, with breadth of mind; through his father's appointment he was made envoy of the Shuofang military commission; he followed his father through Bin and Meng, and when he again held Shuofang, all were made staff posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye was clever and broad-minded as a youth; through his father's influence he became an envoy of the Shuofang commission, followed him through Bin and Meng, and when his father again held Shuofang he held staff posts there.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，暉疾，繼業圖殺其兄繼勳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun in Zhou, Hui fell ill; Jiye plotted to kill his elder brother Jixun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou Guangshun era, when Hui fell ill, Jiye plotted to kill his elder brother Jixun.

sentences.zh: 暉卒，遂代其父為朔方軍留後。

translations.literal: When Hui died, he then replaced his father as acting commissioner of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died he succeeded his father as acting commissioner of the Shuofang Army.

sentences.zh: 以郊祀恩，加靈州大都督府長史，遷朔方節度、靈環觀察、處置、度支、溫池榷稅等使。

translations.literal: Through suburban-sacrifice grace he was made chief administrator of the Lingzhou metropolitan prefecture, and was moved to military commissioner of Shuofang, observation commissioner of Ling and Huan, disposition, revenue, and Wenchi monopoly commissioner, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: By suburban-sacrifice grace he was made chief administrator of Lingzhou and promoted to military commissioner of Shuofang with oversight of Ling and Huan, disposition, revenue, and Wenchi monopoly affairs.

sentences.zh: 恭帝時，繼業既殺兄代父領鎮，頗驕恣，時出兵劫略羌夷，羌夷不附，又撫士卒少恩，繼業慮其為變，以太祖居鎮日常得給事，乃豫徙其孥闕下。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gong, Jiye, having killed his brother and replaced his father in command of the circuit, was quite arrogant and willful, often sending troops to raid Qiang and Yi; the Qiang and Yi did not attach themselves; he also treated troops with little kindness; Jiye feared they would mutiny; because Taizu when stationed in the circuit had often been able to serve him, he beforehand moved their families to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gong, Jiye had killed his brother to seize his father's command and grew arrogant, raiding Qiang and Yi tribes until they would not submit; he also showed little kindness to his troops and, fearing mutiny, moved their families to the capital because Taizu had once served under his father in the same circuit.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，來朝，連以駝馬、寶器為獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong he came to court, repeatedly presenting camels, horses, and precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianlong he came to court bearing camels, horses, and precious goods.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，賜詔獎諭，拜靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao an edict praised and instructed him; he was made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 969 an edict praised him and he was made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，改鎮定國軍，吏民立碑頌其遺愛。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to the Dingguo Army; officials and people erected a stele praising his lingering love.
translations.idiomatic: In 970 he was transferred to the Dingguo Army, where officials and people erected a stele praising his benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初來朝，封梁國公，留京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he came to court, was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, and was kept at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he came to court, was enfeoffed Duke of Liang, and was kept at the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年五十一，贈侍中。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged fifty-one, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year at fifty-one and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王承美

translations.literal: Wang Chengmei
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengmei

sentences.zh: 王承美，豐州人，本河西藏才族都首領。

translations.literal: Wang Chengmei, a native of Fengzhou, was originally chief of the Zangcai tribe in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengmei, a native of Fengzhou, was originally chief of the Zangcai tribe in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 其父事契丹，為左千牛衛將軍，開寶二年，率眾來歸。

translations.literal: His father served the Khitan as general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard; in the second year of Kaibao he led the multitude to come over.
translations.idiomatic: His father had served the Khitan as general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard; in 969 he led his people to defect to the Song.

sentences.zh: 承美授豐州牙內指揮使，父卒，改天德軍蕃漢都指揮使、知州事，移豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Chengmei was appointed inner commander of Fengzhou's guard; when his father died he was changed to commander of the Tiande Army's tribal and Han forces and put in charge of prefectural affairs, then moved to prefect of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmei was made inner commander of the Fengzhou guard; after his father's death he became commander of Tiande's tribal and Han forces and prefect of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣軍校詣闕，言願誘退渾、突厥內附，上嘉其意。

translations.literal: He sent a military officer to the palace, saying he wished to entice the Tuyuhun and Turks of the frontier to come over; the emperor praised his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an officer to court offering to entice the Tuyuhun and Turks on the frontier to submit; the emperor commended his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七年，與契丹戰，斬獲以萬計，禽其天德軍節度使韋太以獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo he fought the Khitan; kills and captures numbered in the tens of thousands; he captured their Tiande Army military commissioner Wei Tai and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: In 982 he fought the Khitan, killing and capturing tens of thousands, and presented their Tiande Army commander Wei Tai as a captive.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹來寇，又擊敗其眾萬餘，追北至青冢百餘里，斬獲益眾。

translations.literal: The next year the Khitan came to raid; he again defeated their host of more than ten thousand, pursued north to Qingzhong for more than a hundred li, and kills and captures grew still more.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Khitan raided again, he routed more than ten thousand of them and pursued north beyond Qingzhong for over a hundred li with still heavier losses to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 以功授本州團練使。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed regimental trainer of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made regimental trainer of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 以乞黨族次首領弗香克浪買為歸德郎將，沒細大首領越移為懷化大將軍，瓦窯為歸德大將軍。

translations.literal: The Qidang tribe's second-ranking leader Fuxiang Kelangmai was made Guide Langjiang; the Meixi great leader Yueyi was made Great General for Pacification; Wayao was made Great Guide General.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Fuxiang Kelangmai, second chief of the Qidang, Guide Langjiang; Yueyi, great chief of Meixi, Great General for Pacification; and Wayao Great Guide General.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年冬來朝，令歸所部，控子河汊。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Chunhua he came to court; he was ordered to return to his command and hold the Zihe fork.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 991 he came to court and was ordered to return to his post and hold the Zihe fork.

sentences.zh: 自是諸蕃歲修貢禮，頗效忠順。

translations.literal: From then on the various tribes annually maintained tribute ritual and showed considerable loyalty and submission.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the frontier tribes paid annual tribute and remained largely loyal.

sentences.zh: 景德初來朝，以其守邊歲久，遷本州防禦使以還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he came to court; because he had long guarded the border, he was promoted to defense commissioner of his prefecture and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era he came to court and, for his long border service, was promoted to defense commissioner of Fengzhou and sent back.

sentences.zh: 自承美內屬，給奉同蕃官例，至是，特詔月增五萬。

translations.literal: From Chengmei's coming over, stipends were given on the tribal-official precedent; at this time a special edict monthly increased fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Since his defection he had been paid on the tribal-official scale; now an edict specially added fifty thousand cash per month.

sentences.zh: 尋請於州城置孔子廟，詔可之。

translations.literal: Soon he asked to set up a Confucius temple in the prefectural city; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon petitioned to build a Confucius temple in the prefectural city, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾被疾，遣中使挾醫視之。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill; the court sent a palace envoy with a physician to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and the court sent a palace envoy with a physician to treat him.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，卒，贈恩州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1012 and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，錄其子文寶、孫懷筠以官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his sons Wenbao and grandson Huaijun were enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1013 his son Wenbao and grandson Huaijun were given official posts.

sentences.zh: 初，承美養其長孫文玉為子，奏署殿直，及卒，其本族首領上言文玉曉達軍政，請令襲承美任。

translations.literal: At first Chengmei had adopted his eldest grandson Wenyu as a son and memorialized to appoint him palace attendant; when he died, chiefs of his native tribe submitted that Wenyu understood military administration and asked that he inherit Chengmei's post.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmei had earlier adopted his eldest grandson Wenyu and appointed him palace attendant; when he died, tribal chiefs petitioned that Wenyu, skilled in military affairs, succeed him.

sentences.zh: 下蕃漢議，議同，以為侍禁、知州事。

translations.literal: It was sent down for tribal and Han deliberation; the deliberation agreed, and he was made palace guard and put in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to tribal and Han councils, which agreed, and Wenyu was made palace guard with charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 文玉父文恭時為侍禁，在沂州，表訴其事，詔改文恭為供奉宮。

translations.literal: Wenyu's father Wengong was then a palace guard at Yizhou; he memorialized to protest the matter; an edict changed Wengong to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu's father Wengong, then a palace guard at Yizhou, protested in a memorial, and an edict made Wengong palace attendant instead.

sentences.zh: 九年，承美葬，詔以帛緡、米麴、羊酒賜其家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Chengmei was buried, an edict granted his family silk cash, rice, leaven, sheep, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: In 1016, at Chengmei's burial, the court granted his family silk, grain, leaven, sheep, and wine.

sentences.zh: 李繼周

translations.literal: Li Jizhou
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhou

sentences.zh: 李繼周，延州金明人。

translations.literal: Li Jizhou was a native of Jinming in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhou was a native of Jinming in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖計都，父孝順，皆為金明鎮使，繼周嗣掌本族。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jidu and father Xiaoshun were both Jinming garrison commissioners; Jizhou succeeded and held his clan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jidu and father Xiaoshun had both been Jinming garrison commissioners, and Jizhou succeeded as head of the clan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，東山蕃落集眾寇清化砦，繼周率眾敗之，殺三千餘人，補殿前承旨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, eastern hill tribal settlements gathered a host to raid Qinghua Fort; Jizhou led troops to defeat them and killed more than three thousand; he was made a palace attendant before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 978 eastern hill tribes massed to raid Qinghua Fort; Jizhou routed them, killing more than three thousand, and was made palace attendant before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，又與侯延廣敗未藏、未腋等族於渾州西山。

translations.literal: In Yongxi he again, with Hou Yanguang, defeated the Weicang and Weiye tribes and others at Western Hill in Hunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he and Hou Yanguang again defeated the Weicang, Weiye, and other tribes at Western Hill in Hunzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，遷殿直，賜介冑、戎器、茶綵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was moved to palace attendant and granted armor, weapons, and tea and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In 993 he was promoted to palace attendant and granted armor, weapons, and gifts of tea and brocade.

sentences.zh: 明年，討李繼遷，命開治塞門、鴉兒兩路，又招降族帳首領二十餘人，率所部入夏州，敗蕃兵數千於石堡砦。

translations.literal: The next year, campaigning against Li Jiqian, he was ordered to open and repair the Saimen and Ya'er routes; he also received the surrender of more than twenty tribal chieftains, led his command into Xiazhou, and defeated several thousand tribal troops at Shibao Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the campaign against Li Jiqian, he opened the Saimen and Ya'er routes, received the surrender of more than twenty tribal chiefs, led his men into Xiazhou, and defeated several thousand Tangut troops at Shibao Fort.

sentences.zh: 以功轉供奉官，復加恩賞，仍賜官第。

translations.literal: For merit he was made a palace attendant, again received favor and reward, and was still granted an official residence.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made palace attendant, rewarded again, and granted an official residence.

sentences.zh: 繼周以阿都關、塞門、盧關等砦最居邊要，遂規修築砦城。

translations.literal: Jizhou, because the forts of Adu Pass, Saimen, and Luguan were most on the frontier's vital points, then planned to repair and build fort cities.
translations.idiomatic: Because the forts at Adu Pass, Saimen, and Luguan were the most critical frontier posts, Jizhou planned to repair and build fortifications there.

sentences.zh: 在磨盧家、媚咩、拽藏等族居近盧關，未嘗內順。

translations.literal: The Molujia, Meime, and Zhuai-cang tribes dwelt near Luguan and had never submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: The Molujia, Meime, and Zhuaicang tribes lived near Luguan and had never submitted.

sentences.zh: 繼周夜率所部往襲，焚之，斬首俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Jizhou by night led his command to raid them, burned them, and beheaded and captured in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou led a night raid on them, burned their settlements, and took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，授西京作坊副使，賜袍帶、銀綵、雕戈以寵之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was made deputy commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and granted robes, belts, silver brocade, and carved halberds to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In 996 he was made deputy commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and honored with robes, belts, silver brocade, and carved halberds.

sentences.zh: 大軍討西夏，命為延州路踏白先鋒。

translations.literal: The great army campaigned against Western Xia; he was ordered to be vanguard scout of the Yanzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army campaigned against Western Xia he was named vanguard scout of the Yanzhou route.

sentences.zh: 會繼遷邀戰於路，繼周戰卻之。

translations.literal: It happened that Jiqian intercepted battle on the road; Jizhou fought and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqian ambushed him on the march, but Jizhou fought him off.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，改西京左藏庫副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was changed to deputy commissioner of the Western Capital left treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he was made deputy commissioner of the Western Capital left treasury.

sentences.zh: 三年，復為先鋒，人賊境，焚積聚，殺人畜，獲器甲凡六十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the third year he again served as vanguard, entered bandit territory, burned stores, killed people and livestock, and captured armor and weapons totaling more than six hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1000 he again served as vanguard, raided deep into enemy territory, burned stores, slaughtered people and livestock, and seized more than six hundred thousand pieces of armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 授供備庫使，領金明縣兵馬都監、新砦解家河盧關路都巡檢。

translations.literal: He was appointed commissioner of the supply depot, held military supervisor of Jinming County and overall inspector of the Xinzai Jiejiahe Luguan route.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of the supply depot, military supervisor of Jinming County, and overall inspector of the Xinzai Jiejiahe Luguan route.

sentences.zh: 五年，授西京作坊使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.
translations.idiomatic: In 1002 he was appointed commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.

sentences.zh: 蕃騎入鈔，繼周逐之出境。

translations.literal: Tribal horsemen entered to raid; Jizhou drove them beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal horsemen raided across the border, Jizhou drove them back out.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，夏人圍麟州，繼周受詔率兵會李繼福掩擊之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde the Xia people besieged Linzhou; Jizhou received an edict to lead troops and join Li Jifu in a flanking strike.
translations.idiomatic: In 1004, when the Tangut besieged Linzhou, Jizhou was ordered to join Li Jifu in a flanking attack.

sentences.zh: 加領誠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally made prefect of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made prefect of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，卒，年六十七，詔邊臣擇其子可襲職者以名聞，邊臣言其子殿直士彬遜愞，從子士用樸忠練邊事，且為部落所伏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged sixty-seven; an edict ordered border officials to choose whichever son could inherit the post and report his name; border officials said his son, palace attendant Shibin, was timid and dull, while his nephew Shiyong was plain, loyal, versed in border affairs, and moreover respected by the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1009 at sixty-seven; the court ordered border officials to name a worthy successor; they reported that his son Shibin was timid and dull but his nephew Shiyong was steadfast, knew frontier affairs, and was respected by the tribes.

sentences.zh: 乃詔士彬管勾部族事，士用為巡檢都監以左右之。

translations.literal: An edict then made Shibin oversee tribal affairs and Shiyong inspection commander to assist him on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Shibin to oversee tribal affairs with Shiyong as inspection commander to support him.

sentences.zh: 士彬後至供備庫副使、金明縣都監、新砦解家河盧關路巡檢。

translations.literal: Shibin later reached deputy commissioner of the supply depot, military supervisor of Jinming County, and inspector of the Xinzai Jiejiahe Luguan route.
translations.idiomatic: Shibin later rose to deputy commissioner of the supply depot, military supervisor of Jinming County, and inspector of the Xinzai Jiejiahe Luguan route.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，元昊反，攻保安軍，而潛兵襲金明，士彬父子俱被禽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, Yuan Hao rebelled, attacked Bao'an Army, and secretly sent troops to strike Jinming; Shibin and his son were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: In 1040, when Yuan Hao rebelled and attacked Bao'an Army while secretly striking Jinming, Shibin and his son were both captured.

sentences.zh: 士彬兄士紹至內殿崇班，士用至供奉官、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Shibin's elder brother Shishao reached inner palace attendant of the honored class; Shiyong reached palace attendant and gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: Shibin's elder brother Shishao rose to honored inner palace attendant; Shiyong became palace attendant and gate usher.

sentences.zh: 李繼福者，亦與繼周同時歸順，授永平砦茭村軍主，以戰功歷歸德將軍，領順州刺史，至內殿崇班、新歸明諸族都巡檢。

translations.literal: Li Jifu also came over at the same time as Jizhou, was appointed garrison chief of Jiaocun at Yongping Fort, through battle merit rose to Guide General, held the prefecture of Shunzhou, and reached inner palace attendant of the honored class and overall inspector of the Newly Submitted Ming tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu, who had submitted at the same time as Jizhou, was made garrison chief of Jiaocun at Yongping Fort, rose through battle to Guide General and prefect of Shunzhou, and eventually became honored inner palace attendant and overall inspector of the newly submitted Ming tribes.

sentences.zh: 孫行友

translations.literal: Sun Xingyou
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingyou

sentences.zh: 孫行友，莫州清苑人，世業農。

translations.literal: Sun Xingyou, a native of Qingyuan in Mozhou, for generations practiced farming.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingyou, a native of Qingyuan in Mozhou, came from a farming family.

sentences.zh: 初，定州西二百里有狼山者，當易州中路，舊有城堡，邊人賴之以避寇。

translations.literal: At first, two hundred li west of Dingzhou was Wolf Mountain, lying on the middle route of Yizhou; formerly there was a castle, and border people relied on it to avoid bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li west of Dingzhou stood Wolf Mountain on the main road to Yizhou; an old fort there had long sheltered border people from raiders.

sentences.zh: 山中蘭若有尼，姓孫氏，名深意，有術惑眾。

translations.literal: In the mountain orchid temple was a nun, surname Sun, name Shenyi, who had arts that deluded the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In a mountain temple lived a nun of the Sun clan named Shenyi, whose occult practices drew a following.

sentences.zh: 行友兄子方諫名之為姑帥，事之甚謹。

translations.literal: Xingyou's elder brother's son Fangjian named her "Aunt Commander" and served her very respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Fangjian, son of Xingyou's elder brother, called her "Aunt Commander" and served her with great deference.

sentences.zh: 及尼坐亡，行友益神其事，因以其術然香燈，聚民漸眾。

translations.literal: When the nun died in custody, Xingyou made her affairs still more miraculous, and by her arts lit incense lamps; the gathering of people gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: After the nun died in custody, Xingyou treated her cult with even greater awe, lighting incense by her rites until his following steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 自晉少帝與契丹絕好，邊州困於轉輸，逋民往往依方諫，推以為帥。

translations.literal: From when Emperor Shaodi of Jin broke with the Khitan, border prefectures were distressed by transport; fugitive people often relied on Fangjian and pushed him to be commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin emperor Shaodi broke with the Khitan, border prefectures groaned under supply burdens, and fugitives often rallied to Fangjian and made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 方諫懼主帥捕逐，乃表歸朝，因署為東北面招收指揮使，且賜院額曰「勝福」。

translations.literal: Fangjian feared the chief commander would capture and drive him out, therefore memorialized to come over to the court, and was appointed northeastern recruiting commander, and moreover granted the monastery plaque "Shengfu."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing arrest by the regional commander, Fangjian submitted to the court, was made northeastern recruiting commander, and received the monastery name Shengfu.

sentences.zh: 每契丹軍來，必率其徒襲擊之，鎧仗、畜產所得漸多，人益依以避難焉。

translations.literal: Whenever Khitan armies came, he was sure to lead his followers to strike them; armor, weapons, and livestock taken gradually increased, and people increasingly relied on him to escape hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Khitan armies appeared he led his men against them, gathering ever more arms and livestock, and refugees increasingly looked to him for safety.

sentences.zh: 易、定帥聞於朝，因以方諫為邊界遊奕使，行友副之。

translations.literal: The commanders of Yi and Ding reported to court, and Fangjian was made border roaming inspector with Xingyou as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi and Ding commanders reported to court, and Fangjian was made border roaming inspector with Xingyou as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 自是捍禦侵軼，多所殺獲。

translations.literal: From then on in defending against raids they killed and captured in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they beat back raids with many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 乘勝入祁溝關、平庸城，破飛狐砦，契丹頗畏之，邊民千餘家賴以無患。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory they entered Qigou Pass and Pingyong City, took Feihu Fort, and the Khitan came to fear them greatly; more than a thousand border households relied on them and were free from trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Following up their victories they took Qigou Pass and Pingyong City and captured Feihu Fort; the Khitan grew to fear them, and more than a thousand border households lived untroubled under their protection.

sentences.zh: 然亦陰持兩端，以圖自固。

translations.literal: Yet they also secretly held both ends to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they also played both sides to secure their own position.

sentences.zh: 已而晉師失律，薊人道契丹陷中原，方諫之密構也。

translations.literal: Before long Jin armies lost discipline; people of Ji said the Khitan had overrun the central plains—it was Fangjian's secret plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jin armies broke discipline; men of Ji said the Khitan overran the heartland through Fangjian's secret collusion.

sentences.zh: 契丹授方諫定州節度，行友易州刺史。

translations.literal: The Khitan appointed Fangjian military commissioner of Dingzhou and Xingyou prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan made Fangjian military commissioner of Dingzhou and Xingyou prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以蕃將耶律忠代方諫於雲州，方諫不受命，歸保狼山。

translations.literal: Soon because the tribal general Yelü Zhong replaced Fangjian at Yunzhou, Fangjian did not accept the order and returned to hold Wolf Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan general Yelü Zhong was sent to replace Fangjian at Yunzhou, Fangjian refused the order and withdrew to Wolf Mountain.

sentences.zh: 契丹北歸，焚劫山中，方諫自狼山率眾復保定州，歸命於漢，授行友易州刺史，行義泰州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Khitan returned north they burned and plundered the mountains; Fangjian from Wolf Mountain led the host to recover Dingzhou and submitted to Han; Xingyou was appointed prefect of Yizhou and Xingyi prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan withdrew north they burned the mountains; Fangjian led his men from Wolf Mountain, recovered Dingzhou, and submitted to the Han; Xingyou was made prefect of Yizhou and Xingyi prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 弟兄掎角以居，寇每入，諸軍鎮閉壘坐視，一無所得。

translations.literal: The brothers supported one another like corner horns; whenever bandits entered, the various army commands closed their walls and sat watching, gaining nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers backed each other like paired horns; whenever raiders came, other garrisons shut their gates and watched, while the enemy gained nothing from them.

sentences.zh: 行友嘗遣都校王友遇巡警於石河，與契丹遇，殺百餘騎，又嘗獲其刺史蔡幅順、清苑令王璉。

translations.literal: Xingyou once sent chief commander Wang Youyu to patrol at Shi River; he met the Khitan and killed more than a hundred horsemen; he also once captured their prefect Cai Fushun and Qingyuan magistrate Wang Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyou once sent Wang Youyu to patrol the Shi River, killed more than a hundred Khitan horsemen, and on another occasion captured their prefect Cai Fushun and Qingyuan magistrate Wang Lian.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，契丹復犯塞，行友禦之，俘殺數百人。

translations.literal: In Qianyou the Khitan again violated the border; Xingyou resisted them and captured and killed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou the Khitan raided again; Xingyou repulsed them and killed or captured several hundred.

sentences.zh: 周太祖北征，行友道獻俘馘人馬以求見，且請自效，廼厚加賜予，留之軍門。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu campaigned north, Xingyou on the road presented captives, severed heads, men and horses to seek an audience, and also asked to offer himself; he was richly rewarded and kept at army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu marched north, Xingyou met him on the road with captives and heads and asked to serve; Taizu rewarded him generously and kept him at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及周祖受命，行友屢上言偵得契丹離合，願得勁兵三千，乘間平定幽州，乃移方諫鎮華州，以行友為定州留後。

translations.literal: When Zhou Zu received the mandate, Xingyou repeatedly submitted that he had spied out Khitan divisions and unions and wished to have three thousand crack troops to seize the moment and pacify Youzhou; Fangjian was then moved to govern Huazhou and Xingyou was made acting commissioner of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou founder took the throne, Xingyou repeatedly reported Khitan movements and asked for three thousand elite troops to seize Youzhou; Fangjian was transferred to Huazhou and Xingyou made acting commissioner of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，正授節鉞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was formally appointed with the seal of command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande he received formal appointment with the seal of command.

sentences.zh: 世宗自河東還，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Shizong returned from Hedong he was made honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong returned from Hedong he was made honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 六年，世宗北征，行友攻下契丹之易州，擒其刺史任欽以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shizong campaigned north; Xingyou attacked and took the Khitan's Yizhou and captured its prefect Ren Qin to present.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xiande, when Shizong campaigned north, Xingyou took the Khitan city of Yizhou and presented its prefect Ren Qin as a captive.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made Tongping Zhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made Tongping Zhangshi.

sentences.zh: 狼山佛舍妖妄愈甚，眾趨之不可禁，行友不自安，累表乞解官歸山，詔不允。

translations.literal: The Buddhist shrine on Wolf Mountain grew ever more wildly heterodox; the multitude rushed to it and could not be forbidden; Xingyou was ill at ease and repeatedly memorialized begging to resign office and return to the mountains; edicts did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wolf Mountain shrine grew ever more fanatical and drew crowds the government could not restrain; uneasy, Xingyou repeatedly asked to resign and return to the mountains, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，乃徙其帑廩，召集丁壯，繕治兵甲，欲還狼山以自固。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he then moved his stores, gathered able-bodied men, repaired weapons and armor, and wished to return to Wolf Mountain to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: In 962 he moved his stores, gathered fighting men, repaired arms, and prepared to return to Wolf Mountain to fortify himself.

sentences.zh: 兵馬都監藥繼能密表其事，太祖遣閣門副使武懷節馳騎會鎮、趙之兵，稱巡邊，直入其城，行友不之覺。

translations.literal: Military supervisor Yao Jineng secretly memorialized the matter; Taizu sent deputy gate envoy Wu Huaijie with swift horse to join the troops of Zhen and Zhao, claiming a border tour, and entered his city straight in; Xingyou did not perceive it.
