translations.idiomatic: Military supervisor Yao Jineng reported him secretly; Taizu sent Wu Huaijie at speed with Zhen and Zhao troops, ostensibly on a border inspection, and entered the city before Xingyou knew.

sentences.zh: 既而出詔示之，令舉族赴闕，行友蒼黃聽命。

translations.literal: Then an edict was produced and shown him, ordering the whole clan to come to court; Xingyou in panic obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then shown ordering his whole clan to court, and Xingyou obeyed in panic.

sentences.zh: 既至，命侍御史李維岳就第鞫之，得實，下詔切責，削奪從前官爵。

translations.literal: When he arrived, investigating censor Li Weiyue was sent to his residence to examine him; the facts were obtained; an edict sharply rebuked him and stripped his former ranks and titles.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital investigating censor Li Weiyue examined him at home, found the charges true, and an edict stripped his former ranks after a sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 勒歸私第。

translations.literal: He was ordered back to a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was confined to a private residence.

sentences.zh: 仍戮其部下數人，遣使馳詣狼山，輦其尼師之屍焚之。

translations.literal: Still several of his subordinates were executed; an envoy was sent swiftly to Wolf Mountain to cart the nun's corpse and burn it.
translations.idiomatic: Several of his followers were executed, and an envoy was sent to Wolf Mountain to burn the nun's corpse.

sentences.zh: 行友弟易州刺史方進、兄子保塞軍使全暉皆詣闕待罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: Xingyou's younger brother Fangjin, prefect of Yizhou, and elder brother's son Quanhui, commissioner of Bao'sai Army, all came to court to await punishment; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fangjin, prefect of Yizhou, and nephew Quanhui, commissioner of Bao'sai Army, came to court to await punishment and were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，詔免行友禁錮。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year an edict freed Xingyou from confinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year an edict ended his confinement.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以郊祀恩，起為右龍武軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before long, through suburban-sacrifice grace, he was raised as general of the Right Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, by suburban-sacrifice grace, he was restored as general of the Right Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，遷右監門衛大將軍，又改左龍武軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he was moved to great general of the Right Gate Guard, and again changed to great general of the Left Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 964 he became great general of the Right Gate Guard, then of the Left Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，卒，年八十，贈左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he died, aged eighty, and was posthumously made upper general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 981 at eighty and was posthumously made upper general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 方進至德州刺史。

translations.literal: Fangjin reached prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fangjin rose to prefect of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 子全照。

translations.literal: Son: Quanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Quanzhao

sentences.zh: 子 全照

translations.literal: Son: Quanzhao
translations.idiomatic: Son: Quanzhao

sentences.zh: 全照，字繼明，以蔭補殿直，雍熙中授京南巡檢，俄隸幽州部署曹彬麾下，遷供奉官、閣門祗候歷靜戎、威虜二軍監軍。

translations.literal: Quanzhao, style Jiming, through yin privilege was made palace attendant; in Yongxi he was appointed southern capital inspector, soon attached to Youzhou deployment under Cao Bin, moved to palace attendant and gate usher, and served as military supervisor of Jingrong and Weilü armies.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao, courtesy name Jiming, entered service by yin privilege as palace attendant; in Yongxi he became southern capital inspector, soon served under Cao Bin at Youzhou, and became palace attendant and gate usher, supervising the Jingrong and Weilü armies.

sentences.zh: 從田重進擊賊有功，就加西京作坊使，兼知威虜軍，連為廣韶、鄜延二路都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Following Tian Zhongjin in striking bandits he had merit; he was thereupon made commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and given concurrent charge of Weilü Army, and in succession was overall inspector of the Guang-Shao and Fu-Yan routes.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Tian Zhongjin with distinction, was made commissioner of the Western Capital workshops with charge of Weilü Army, and later served as overall inspector on the Guang-Shao and Fu-Yan routes.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，率兵與李繼隆克綏州，因與張崇貴等同戍守之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he led troops with Li Jilong to take Suizhou, and together with Zhang Chonggui and others garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: In 994 he led troops with Li Jilong to capture Suizhou and garrisoned it with Zhang Chonggui and others.

sentences.zh: 俄護屯兵於夏州，兼知州事。

translations.literal: Soon he guarded garrison troops at Xiazhou and concurrently governed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He soon guarded troops at Xiazhou with concurrent charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召還，為登萊路都巡檢使，遷左藏庫使、延州監軍兼阿都關盧關路都巡檢事。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was made overall inspector of the Deng-Lai route, moved to commissioner of the left treasury and military supervisor of Yanzhou with overall inspection of the Adu Pass and Luguan route.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became overall inspector of the Deng-Lai route, then commissioner of the left treasury and Yanzhou military supervisor with oversight of the Adu and Luguan route.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，人掌軍頭引見司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he entered to head the Army Head Presentation Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he took charge of the Army Head Presentation Office.

sentences.zh: 二年，加如京使，為涇原路鈐轄兼安撫都監，是冬徙幷、汾等州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made envoy like to the capital, Jingyuan route commander and pacification overall supervisor; that winter he was moved to overall inspector of Bing, Fen, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In 999 he became envoy like to the capital, Jingyuan commander and pacification supervisor, and that winter overall inspector of Bing, Fen, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 三年，改知順安軍，代還，復為環慶路鈐轄，與李繼和規度靈州道路。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to command Shun'an Army; when replaced and returned, he again became Huanqing route commander and with Li Jihe surveyed the road to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1000 he was made commander of Shun'an Army; on returning from replacement he again commanded Huanqing and surveyed the Lingzhou road with Li Jihe.

sentences.zh: 四年，加西上閣門使，復為環慶路鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made western upper gate envoy and again Huanqing route commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1001 he was made western upper gate envoy and again Huanqing route commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，將城綏州，以慕興為綏州路部署，全照為鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year they were about to fortify Suizhou; Mu Xing was made Suizhou route deployment commissioner and Quanzhao commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1002, when Suizhou was to be fortified, Mu Xing was made route deployment commissioner and Quanzhao commander.

sentences.zh: 既又慮全照素剛執，與興不協，乃以曹璨代之。

translations.literal: Then, fearing that Quanzhao by nature was stubborn and obstinate and would not harmonize with Xing, Cao Shen was used to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Quanzhao's stubborn nature would clash with Mu Xing, the court replaced him with Cao Shen.

sentences.zh: 既調兵夫二萬餘，全照言其非便，乃罷。

translations.literal: When more than twenty thousand labor troops had been mobilized, Quanzhao said it was not expedient, and it was then abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty thousand laborers were mobilized, Quanzhao protested that the plan was impractical and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 又嘗命度地河北，全照言沿河高阜可分置城堡屯戍者，寧邊軍南、武強縣側凡二處，上重於興役，止命營安平南，徙置祁州。

translations.literal: He was also once ordered to survey land in Hebei; Quanzhao said that along the river on high mounds one could separately set castles and garrison colonies—south of Ningbian Army and beside Wuqiang County, two places in all; the emperor, weighing the labor, only ordered a camp south of Anping and moved Qi Prefecture there.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to survey Hebei, Quanzhao proposed garrison castles on high ground along the river at two sites south of Ningbian Army and beside Wuqiang County; the emperor, wary of the labor, only built south of Anping and moved Qi Prefecture there.

sentences.zh: 俄知天雄軍府。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，上裁定防秋禦戎之要，命為寧邊軍部署，領兵八千扼要害之路。

translations.literal: In the sixth summer the emperor settled the essentials of autumn defense against barbarians and ordered him deployment commissioner of Ningbian Army, leading eight thousand troops to block the vital routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth summer the emperor fixed autumn defense policy and made him deployment commissioner of Ningbian Army with eight thousand men to hold the critical passes.

sentences.zh: 以全照好陵人，取其嘗所保薦者王德鈞、裴自榮共事焉。

translations.literal: Because Quanzhao liked to bully people, those he had once recommended and vouched for—Wang Dejun and Pei Zirong—were taken to serve with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Quanzhao was overbearing, the emperor assigned Wang Dejun and Pei Zirong, whom he had once recommended, to serve with him.

sentences.zh: 全照形短精悍，知兵，以嚴毅整眾，然性剛使氣，專任刑罰。

translations.literal: Quanzhao was short in stature, keen and brave, understood warfare, and by stern discipline ordered the multitude; yet his nature was stubborn and he vented his temper, relying solely on punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao was short, tough, and skilled in war, ruling his men with stern discipline, yet he was headstrong, quick to anger, and ruled through punishment alone.

sentences.zh: 中書初進擬嚴州刺史，上曰：「全照深刻，常慮人以嚴察議己，今授此州，似涉譏誚。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat at first advanced him as prefect of Yanzhou; the emperor said: "Quanzhao is harsh; he constantly fears people will discuss him as severe and scrutinizing—now to grant this prefecture seems to touch on ridicule."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat first proposed him for Yanzhou; the emperor said, "Quanzhao is harsh and fears being called severe—making him prefect of Yanzhou would look like mockery."

sentences.zh: 乃改焉。

translations.literal: It was then changed.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was changed.

sentences.zh: 三年，為邠寧環慶都部署。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made overall deployment commissioner of Binning and Huanqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made overall deployment commissioner of Binning and Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 趙德明納款，朝議減西鄙戍兵，令屯近地，全照以邊防不可無備，未即奉詔。

translations.literal: Zhao Deming submitted allegiance; court discussion wished to reduce western border garrison troops and order them stationed in nearby places; Quanzhao held that the border defense could not be without preparation and did not immediately obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Deming submitted allegiance, the court proposed reducing western garrisons and moving troops closer in; Quanzhao held the frontier could not go unguarded and delayed obeying.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「全照是好勇多言者。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Quanzhao is one who loves bravery and speaks much.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Quanzhao is bold and talkative.

sentences.zh: 德明使已至闕，復何慮焉？」

translations.literal: Deming's envoy has already reached court—what is there to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Deming's envoy is already at court—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 因徙全照知永興軍府，仍拜四方館使。

translations.literal: He therefore moved Quanzhao to govern Yongxing Army and still made him commissioner of the Four Directions Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore transferred Quanzhao to Yongxing Army and made him commissioner of the Four Directions Hall.

sentences.zh: 西師移屯者至府，命全照兼駐泊鈐轄。

translations.literal: When western troops moved to garrison reached the prefecture, Quanzhao was ordered to concurrently serve as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: When western troops redeployed to the prefecture, Quanzhao was made their garrison commander as well.

sentences.zh: 全照許州有別墅，求典是州，可之。

translations.literal: Quanzhao had a villa in Xuzhou; he asked to govern that prefecture, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao owned a villa in Xuzhou, asked to govern that prefecture, and was granted his request.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，遷引進使。

translations.literal: In Dazhong Xiangfu he was moved to commissioner of presentation.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong Xiangfu he was made commissioner of presentation.

sentences.zh: 逾歲表求歸朝，命掌閣門、客省、四方館事。

translations.literal: After a year he memorialized asking to return to court and was ordered to manage gate, guest, and Four Directions Hall affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he asked to return to court and was put in charge of the gate, guest, and Four Directions offices.

sentences.zh: 四年，車駕西幸，留為新城都巡檢，未幾，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the imperial carriage went west, he was left as overall inspector of Xincheng; before long he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the emperor traveled west, he was left overall inspector of Xincheng; he died soon after at sixty.

sentences.zh: 論曰：五代之季，邊圉之不靖也久矣。

translations.literal: The comment says: At the end of the Five Dynasties, the borderlands had long been unquiet.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: At the end of the Five Dynasties the frontier had long been unsettled.

sentences.zh: 太祖之興，雖不勤遠略，而向之陸梁跋扈而不可制者，莫不竭忠效節，雖奔走僵仆而不避，豈人心之有異哉？

translations.literal: When Taizu rose, though he did not labor at distant strategy, those who before had been violent, arrogant, and uncontrollable all exhausted loyalty and offered integrity; though they ran and fell stiff they did not avoid it—how could human hearts be different?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu rose, though he did not pursue distant conquests, men who had once been violent and ungovernable now served with loyal zeal, facing death without flinching—was human nature itself so different?

sentences.zh: 良由威德之並用，控御之有道也。

translations.literal: It was truly because awe and virtue were used together and control and restraint were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, awe and kindness worked together, and control was exercised with skill.

sentences.zh: 折氏據有府谷，與李彜興之居夏州，初無以異。

translations.literal: The Zhe clan held Fugu, and Li Yixing's dwelling in Xiazhou—at first there was no difference.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe held Fugu as Li Yixing held Xiazhou—at first there was little difference between them.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其嚮化，許以世襲，雖不無世卿之嫌，自從阮而下，繼生名將，世篤忠貞，足為西北之捍，可謂無負於宋者矣。

translations.literal: Taizu praised their turning to civilization and permitted hereditary succession; though there was not without the suspicion of hereditary ministers, from Congruan downward they continuously produced famous generals, generation after generation devoted and loyal, sufficient as bulwarks of the northwest—one may say they did not fail Song.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu honored their submission and allowed hereditary rule; though that invited the suspicion of a hereditary fief, from Congruan onward the family produced famous generals generation after generation, loyal bulwarks of the northwest who did not fail the Song.

sentences.zh: 承美、繼周，分蒞種落，亦能世其職者也。

translations.literal: Chengmei and Jizhou, each presiding over tribal settlements, also could pass down their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmei and Jizhou, each overseeing tribal peoples, likewise passed their offices from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 繼業雖出賊叛之族，而有循良之風。

translations.literal: Jiye, though he came from a clan of bandit rebels, had the manner of the orderly and good.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye came from a rebel house yet showed a measure of orderly governance.

sentences.zh: 方諫、行友介遼、晉間，持兩端以取將相，終以首鼠獲咎，其諸異端之害歟？

translations.literal: Fangjian and Xingyou stood between Liao and Jin, held both ends to obtain minister and general rank, and in the end were blamed for wavering like a rat—was this not the harm of heterodox ways?
translations.idiomatic: Fangjian and Xingyou, caught between Liao and Jin, played both sides for high office and in the end were ruined by their wavering—was this not the cost of double-dealing?

sentences.zh: 全照職親禁衛，素稱嚴果，而昧於弭兵之利，君子所不予也。

translations.literal: Quanzhao's post was close to the palace guard; he was always called stern and resolute, yet he was blind to the benefit of ending war—the gentleman does not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao served in the inner guard, was known for stern resolve, yet failed to see the value of peace—the judgment of the historians withholds full praise.
